title: feat: open a project read-only with --read-only and open_project read_only
body:
## What changed

`camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens a project read-only. The MCP
tool `open_project` takes `read_only: true` for the same result. A save
over the opened file is then refused on every save route, and the file
stays byte for byte. A save to another file works and ends read-only. The
title bar shows `CamCraft - job.camproj (read-only)`.

- One rule, `project::refuse_read_only_save` in `crates/app/src/project/`,
  refuses a save to the file that the project is open read-only from. The
  window's `State::save_project_path` and `script::api::v_save` call it.
  `v_save` serves MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live MCP
  seam of a window.
- The rule compares canonical paths, so a save from the Save As dialog
  to the opened file is refused too.
- In the window, Save on a read-only project opens the Save As dialog, as
  the editor for shipped machines does. The Save of the unsaved-changes
  prompt does the same.
- Changes stay allowed in memory.
- The read-only state is kept next to the document path:
  `State::project_read_only` in the window, `Env::doc_read_only` in a
  headless MCP session or a script run. The live seam gets the window's
  state through `LiveOptions::read_only`.
- A model file with `--read-only` is imported as usual. A headless start
  ignores the option. The live seam still refuses `open_project`.
- The same option name and behaviour as the open SolidCraft proposal
  for `--read-only` (tangency-labs/solidcraft#20830).
- No change to the file format or `PROJECT_VERSION`.
- Docs: the `--help` text, `docs/user-guide/start-options.md`,
  `site/content/guide/automate/cli.md` and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3609-read-only-open.md`.

This branch starts at upstream/main `60b19abe8`. Two merges of upstream
main follow it: `b94dcd378` (main `82db54282`) and `98cd5b28b` (main
`3fc0e017b`). There is no rebase.

- The first merge had conflicts with #3608 (overwrite guard) and #3584
  (start options). Both sides added lines in the same places. The merge
  keeps both sides.
- In `v_save` and `State::save_project_path`, the read-only check runs
  first, and then the overwrite guard of #3608. Thus `overwrite: true`
  does not write over a file that is open read-only.
- `--read-only` comes after `--no-activate` and `--minimized` in the
  options table, the `--help` text and `start-options.md`.
  `run_windowed` takes the start mode and `read_only`.
- `LiveOptions` and `Env` have `read_only` and `doc_stamp`. The
  `save_project` description has the sentences of both changes.
- `crates/app/tests/save_overwrite_guard.rs` gets one line,
  `read_only: false`, in its `LiveOptions` value. This is the only line
  outside the files of this change.
- The second merge had no conflicts. It brings in #3687 (a relative
  model link resolves against the project folder).

## Tests

New in `crates/app/tests/read_only_open.rs`:

- `the_rule_refuses_only_the_opened_file_of_a_read_only_project`
- `a_read_only_project_refuses_a_save_over_its_file_and_keeps_it`
- `a_save_to_another_file_works_and_ends_read_only`
- `a_plain_open_ends_read_only_and_a_bad_flag_changes_nothing`
- `a_script_save_after_a_read_only_open_is_refused`
- `the_live_seam_refuses_an_approved_save_over_a_read_only_window_project`

New in `crates/ui/src/launch_file_tests.rs`:

- `a_read_only_project_refuses_a_save_over_its_file_and_save_as_ends_read_only`
- `read_only_changes_nothing_for_a_model_file`

New in `crates/ui/src/cli_options_tests.rs`:

- `read_only_is_a_switch_that_keeps_the_file_after_it`

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head `98cd5b28b`
(Windows 11). The diff since main `3fc0e017b` is 23 files. 226 of 229
steps passed, and 0 stalled. The three red steps are not from this
change:

- `example_catalog`: `catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::{rebuilds,regenerates}`.
  The refusal text is equal, and only the line end is different. The
  checkout uses `core.autocrlf=true`, so `refusal.txt` has `\r\n`.
- `catalog_render`: `catalog_cases_open_and_frame_cleanly`. The case
  `3d/rough-finish` links `model/rough-finish.obj`. With
  `core.autocrlf=true` the file on disk has `\r\n`, so its sha256 is not
  the one in the project, and the link check imports it again. The blob
  in git has the sha256 of the project.
- `first_router_part`:
  `first_router_part_project_loads_verifies_and_posts_to_grblhal`. Main
  is red with this step (#3698).

The steps of this change and of #3608 all passed:

- `read_only_open`: 6 passed.
- `save_overwrite_guard`: 7 passed.
- `mcp_live`: 14 passed.
- `mcp_doc_drift`: 6 passed.
- `mcp`: 29 passed.
- `scripting`: 20 passed.
- `project_roundtrip`: 80 passed.
- `first_part_programs`: 2 passed (#3574 is fixed on main).
- The app lib tests: 303 passed.
- The `camcraft-ui` lib tests: 1524 passed, 8 ignored. These include
  `launch_file_tests` and `cli_options_tests`.
- 15 of the 16 ui suites passed, among them `gpu_render`, `shell` and
  `operations`. The red one is `catalog_render` (above).

The other app steps are the suites that the gate maps from
`app::project`, `app::script` and `app::mcp`.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
on `98cd5b28b`: clean (exit 0). The only warning is the manifest note about the unused workspace dependency `truck-polymesh`, which is not from this change.
Heavy lanes: not run (no heavy step for a `P2` or lower PR, #3556).
Reach from `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` at `144d07a85`: every `app`
heavy target (212 steps), because `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs` changed.

## Manual check

Windows 11, debug build of `98cd5b28b`. A person did the keyboard and
dialog steps. The window title and the files were read through Windows
and on disk.

1. `camcraft-ui --read-only edge-work.camproj`, a copy of
   `examples/catalog/2d/edge-work`. The title is
   `CamCraft - edge-work.camproj (read-only)`. The status line says
   `opened ... (read-only; Save As writes your own copy)`. The file does
   not change.
2. Ctrl+S opens the Save As dialog.
3. Save As to the same file: Windows asks to replace the file, and the
   user selects yes. CamCraft refuses the save. The status line shows
   `save refused: ... is open read-only; write your copy to a different
   file` in red. The file does not change: the sha256 and the
   modification time are the same.
4. A change to the machine sets the unsaved mark `*` in the title. The
   change stays in memory.
5. Save As to a new file writes `edge-work-copy.camproj`. The title
   becomes `CamCraft - edge-work-copy.camproj`, without `(read-only)` and
   without `*`. The first file does not change.

Finding, not changed in this PR: after the user says yes to the replace
prompt, the user expects a write. The refusal shows only on the status
line, and a narrow window cuts the line. The user in this check did not
see the refusal. A possible follow-up is a notice that the user must
close.

## Not in this change

- A read-only open on the live seam. The live seam refuses
  `open_project`, so that an agent cannot skip the window's
  unsaved-changes prompt. The window's read-only state still reaches a
  live `save_project`.
- A new script form `cam.load(path, options)`. Scripts use
  `cam.call("open_project", {path, read_only: true})`.
- `read_only` in `get_job`.
- The window does not follow the path of a live `save_project` with a
  new path. This is the behaviour today. The window keeps its path and
  stays read-only.
- A reopen from the recent list, or in a later session, is not
  read-only. The recent list keeps paths only.
- The read-only bit of the file on disk.
- A hand-off of the flag to a running window. CamCraft has no
  single-instance hand-off.

## Not exercised

- An automated test of the Save As dialog route in the window. A
  headless test cannot open a native dialog. The tests pin the refusal
  behind it, and the manual check above did the route by hand.
- The live seam through a real window and the AI chat's Allow prompt.
  A test calls `answer_live_with` with the options that the window builds.
- Linux and macOS.
- A project on a network share.
- No test sets a project read-only and then calls `save_project` with
  `overwrite: true` over its own file. The order of the two checks
  (read-only first) is in the code, but no test pins it.

Changelog: `camcraft-ui --read-only` and `open_project` with `read_only: true` open a project read-only: Save never writes over the opened file, and Save As writes your own copy.
Effort: medium

Fixes #3609
